metrics.outcome: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.
metrics.brief: Make a website for Riverside Run 2027, a city running event in Pune. Runners should be able to compare the three races, work out what they will pay with a fee calculator, register with a form, see the race-day and expo-day schedule, see the route and water stations for each race, read FAQs, and see sponsors by tier. Volunteers should be able to sign up with a separate form. Add a countdown to race day, a menu that stays on screen and shows which section you are in, and a high-contrast mode that works across the whole page. It should feel sporty and clear and work well on phones.

review.verdict: The department delivered a workable site in 2 cycles inside the raised budget (222 of 230), with all 15 done-when items and all 8 necessary conditions met at v23 [145], but about a third of the spend (72 of 222 credits) went on fixing avoidable errors such as invented content.

identity.note: Asked the Requester one clear question about T-shirt sizes instead of guessing [78], and gave a decision-ready budget choice [122]. Drifted from role by prescribing the fix wording ('Choose a race to see your total') [127] and detailed fixes [82]. Also missed the missing size list when recording the charter.

adaptation.note: Accepted Priority's counter within 2 attempts [86] and kept fixes small. Did not flag that the registration form needed a size list nobody supplied. The W-1 before W-5 order forced a fallback CTA and a later rework (W-17). The first W-21 proposal was rejected by the validator [128]. Accepted the over-60 KB file [129].

priority.note: Granted 13 at rate-card minimum with a 50 reserve [9]. Its counter was reasoned, but the F-20 it parked came back as F-23 in cycle 2 [85]. It rewrote W-21's steps itself [130], which is design work the role file forbids. 24 near-identical 'within limits' turns.

coordination.note: Stated its scheduling rule every time. Holds named the exact missing condition [44]. Ordering W-2 after the section targets avoided a second failed link check [17]. Repeated the same unresolved CTA note about nine times without an owner acting [17, 26, 30, 44, 49, 54, 59, 64, 69].

audit.note: Found the invented sizes, invented badges, fee-form destination, covered countdown labels, and the 'SECONDS' wrap, each with a finding id [77, 121]. Said plainly that high-contrast was checked in code only [145].

W-17.note: Static CTA and countdown moved into the hero. Label wrap remained for the next fix [121].

W-18.note: Gallery link added, but its note on highlight order is garbled [101]. Menu order differs from page order [145].

W-19.note: Covering problem fixed [96]. Visual check of high-contrast still missing.

W-20.note: Total blank until a race is chosen, rules kept [135].

W-21.note: Labels and title fixed, confirmed by Audit [145]. Its own report only said 'should' [140].

went_well: 0 failed workflows, 0 redirects, 0 invalid moves, 0 role refusals. Estimates matched charges on all 21 workflows.
The Adaptation vs Priority conflict settled itself in 2 attempts, with no escalation [85, 86].
Code checks caught real defects early: the #register link [13], the missing submit button [23], the FAQ tap target [40].
Audit stopped three invented-content or layout problems from shipping [77, 121]. Identity asked the Requester instead of keeping the invented sizes [78].
problems: Invented content got in twice (sizes [29], badges [48]) despite the charter rule, and was caught only at the first Audit [77].
The fix reserve of 50 ran out at v21 with 2 credits left [122]. Rework was 72 of 222 credits (32%) and forced a Requester pause.
The N6 check flagged Rs 270, which Identity confirmed is correct [127]. This looks like a checker false positive. It forced a UX change (W-20) and extra audit rounds.
The file grew from 62 KB (v11) to 81 KB against the ~60 KB rule. It drew 13 warnings and no owner acted [53, 129].
Role drift: Priority rewrote proposal steps [130], where team.md says rejected proposals go back to Adaptation. Identity prescribed the fix text [127]. Code did not catch either.
Priority and Coordination took 45 of 80 turns for 21 builds, mostly repeated 'within limits' handoffs and the same CTA note.
High-contrast was judged from code only [145]. W-13 and W-8 added or changed markup partly to satisfy a check [72, 43].
Lessons were off (memory false, none saved), so the 'save a lesson after a confirmed fix' step went untested.
learnings: Make Identity list missing option lists (sizes) as to-be-confirmed at J2.a, and add a builder rule: report a missing fact to Coordination, do not invent it. Test: rerun with sizes absent and see whether W-5 flags it. Evidence [29, 78].
Run N6 (no invented content) as a per-workflow code check, not only after the last build. It would have caught W-5 and W-9 at once. Evidence [76].
Fix the test system's N6 so it allows values derived from the charter's formulas, such as Rs 270. Evidence [120, 127].
Set the fix reserve from observed rework (about 30% here), not a fixed 50. Test 30% on the next brief. Evidence [122].
Either enforce the 60 KB limit in the validator (one trim step in W-13) or drop it. Warnings nobody owns are noise. Evidence: 13 warnings.
Batch Priority and Coordination handoffs when runs are within limits, and keep hold messages. Test: compare turns and AI calls. Savings unmeasured.
Add a rendered high-contrast check (toggle on, measure contrast) so that done-when item is not verified from code alone.
Route validator rejections to Adaptation, as team.md says, and keep Priority and Identity from rewriting proposals.
Evidence is thin: one brief, one run, Sonnet, memory off. Do not generalise the 32% rework or the turn counts.
